documents.title: AR 5500.1 Standards of Academic Conduct (2024-25 version)
documents.summary: A marked-up draft of the district academic-conduct regulation. Its only AI content is a single listed violation: using AI tools against the policy in the class syllabus or course content. The college sets no AI rule itself and leaves the rule to each instructor.
documents.stance_why: The only AI text, "Violating the instructor’s AI policy as stated on their class syllabus and/or course content", sets no ban or permission and hands the decision to instructors, so the stance is delegates.

units.why: The definition of academic dishonesty lists "Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools" use "that violates the policy stated in class syllabus" as a violation, so unauthorized AI use is classed as academic dishonesty. P36 fits because it classifies improper AI use as misconduct; the actor is the student and the phase is when-misuse because the item defines what counts as a violation.
units.anchor: Useing of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools I that violates the policy stated in class
units.frag_start: Useing of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools
units.policy: Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in a way that violates the policy stated in the class syllabus is academic dishonesty.

units.why: The clause makes "the instructor's AI policy as stated on their class syllabus and/or course content" (canvas page, assignment instructions) the operative rule, so the college sets no AI rule itself and defers to each instructor. P04 fits (instructor-level rule); P06 does not because no fallback for a silent syllabus is stated.
units.anchor: Violating the instructor’s AI policy as stated ion their class syllabus and/or
units.frag_start: Violating the instructor’s AI policy
units.fit_note: Also names where the instructor's AI policy may be stated (canvas page, assignment, exam or assessment instructions), which P04 does not capture.

documents.title: AR 3775 Acceptable Use of Generative AI (draft as of 04/23/2026)
documents.summary: A draft district regulation on acceptable AI use by employees and other authorized users. It allows approved AI tools with human oversight, bans putting sensitive data into unapproved tools, requires disclosure and training, and assigns governance to the IT vice president. It does not govern students, who are sent to the academic-integrity rules.
documents.stance_why: The regulation says "Authorized users may use approved AI tools" under conditions, with listed prohibitions, so it permits AI use with conditions, but only for employees; students are left to "academic integrity and student conduct" rules.

units.why: The Purpose says AI "has the potential to enhance instructional quality, operational efficiency, innovation, and decision-making", a statement of benefits with no rule, so P87 (benefits) and informs.

AR 3775 is a draft covering employees only.
